correctness.rationale: The finite Hankel coefficient matrix and normalized-kernel image were reconstructed explicitly. The top singular value is (s+sqrt(s²+4t²))/2; after unit-norm scaling s=1-t². The exact universal identity F_t(t/2)-25/27=(8-3t²)(3t²-2)²/432 and the exact sharpness factorization at t=sqrt(2/3) were independently expanded symbolically over Q(sqrt6). Both are nonnegative on their stated closed domains with the correct equality locations. Norm upper bound and monomial-only norming-kernel equality follow from the compact rank-two matrix argument. All quantifiers include t=0,1, complex phases, and zero-symbol exemption from ratios. The packaged Python checker performs exact polynomial identities and 2006 assertions; finite spot tests are not used as proof.

originality.rationale: The new contribution is a sharp family-wide minimax constant and complete optimizer coefficient ratio for degree-two Hardy Hankel kernel testing. Dyakonov 2026 and a public monomial-rigidity theorem already establish the qualitative zero-deficit classification, which is not re-claimed. The strongest close finite-rank classification also concerns exact kernel equality, and the exact ratio for a nonpolynomial Hilbert Hankel matrix is an unrelated fixed infinite-rank case. Searches in published-finding corpus and relevant literature did not identify the 25/27 theorem; an older more general rank-two norm equivalence theorem remains a genuine priority risk.

value.rationale: Exact sharp uniform norm-detection guarantee in the smallest natural nonmonomial polynomial Hankel class directly motivated by the 2026 SRKT counterexample. Provides a complete coefficient-level minimax classification and tight 5/(3sqrt3) testing guarantee, not a selected isolated numerical example or a restatement of monomial-only qualitative rigidity. The exact optimal constant and optimizer describe the intrinsic limit of kernel tests for rank-two polynomial symbols and furnish a reproducible benchmark for higher-degree testing questions; no downstream theorem is claimed.
